items.t: 69% Upside for Affirm? Citi Thinks So, and Here’s How
items.sum: Key TakeawaysAffirm is down 23% from its July high after a quarter of fast growth and higher late payments. Citi kept its Buy rating and its $115 target, 69% above today’s price.

items.t: Affirm Printed a “No-Apologies Quarter” and Still Lost 16% in a Month. BMO Sees 53% Upside
items.sum: Key TakeawaysAffirm shares fell 16% in the past month as a hot inflation report, a post-midterm sell-off and credit warnings from Upstart and Block hit consumer lenders. Affirm’s fiscal first quarter beat its own guidance on volume, revenue and revenue less transaction costs, and it raised its full-year GMV outlook to more than $65.

items.t: AFRM Q3 CY2026 deep dive: growth, underwriting, and evolving product mix reshape outlook
items.sum: Buy now, pay later company Affirm (NASDAQ:AFRM) reported revenue ahead of Wall Street’s expectations in calendar Q3 2026 (fiscal Q1 2027), with sales up 35.2% year on year to $1.26 billion. Guidance for next quarter’s revenue was better than expected at $1.45 billion at the midpoint, 1.1% above analysts’ estimates. Its GAAP profit of $0.47 per share was 22.7% above analysts’ consensus estimates.
